findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The blue container for holding ice scoop in the women’s locker was observed to have water and soil accumulation.
2. Dust accumulation was observed in an unsealed opening behind the hood light fixtures.

The inspector instructed the person-in-charge to ensure the non-food contact surfaces are cleaned and kept free of dust, water and soil accumulations.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed kitchen cooler gaskets to be in a state of disrepair. Discussed with PIC, gaskets will be replaced. Ensure equipment is working to meet manufactures standards
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish puck registered 154F at today’s inspection. The dish machine rinse temperature is reading 133F on the integrated thermometer. The breaker to the machines water booster heater has been turned off as the garbage disposal is in the same circuit and the garbage disposal is malfunctioning. The electricity to the dish machine must be left on so that the machine runs at the proper temperature to sanitizer equipment. The equipment and utensils can also be sanitized using the 3 part sink and proper concentration of sanitizer for the appropriate contact time. The items washed today will be rewashed in the dish machine. The machine is now functioning as the booster heater is working now that the circuit breaker was turned back on. The dish puck is now reading 166F.  The violation is considered corrected on site. If the electricity to the booster heater must be turned off, the dishes and equipment must be sanitized in the 3 part sink. Management is now going to require a daily log for dish puck temperature to ensure that the machine is running properly. 

Ensure that the dish puck is run daily to verify that the machine is functioning properly. 

4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
At the snack counter, the inspector noted a spray bottle of cleaner in a cabinet next to food related items. A container of sanitizer wiped is observed next to the coffee making supplies in a different base cabinet. The facility manager moved the items immediately. The employee working at this area was coached concerning this matter. The violation is considered corrected on site. Store chemicals in the open cabinet under the cash register with other chemical cleaners. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. 

Inspector observed a personal lunch box and soda stored in a coolers. Provide separate space in a cooler or separate cold holding unit for employee belongings.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-204.11: A HANDWASHING SINK shall be located: (A) To allow convenient use by EMPLOYEES in FOOD preparation, FOOD dispensing, and WAREWASHING areas (B) In, or immediately adjacent to, toilet rooms. 
Facility is in the middle of replacing the floor in the kitchen. All equipment has been removed from the kitchen and food preparation is taking place in the dry storage area which has smooth cleanable floors walls and ceilings. The employees are washing hands in the restroom before going to the food preparation area. Hand washing stations must be set up in the food prep and the dish washing areas. The facility has until tomorrow’s preparation activities to provide some sort of temporary hand washing facilities at the food prep area and dish washing area. Temporary hand washing includes free flowing hand sink, soap, disposable towels and a catch bucket for the waste water. Also, self contained hand washing stations can be purchased or rented. Provide proper hand washing if the facility intends to continue food service. The administration is going to make a determination today as to whether or not the food service will continue during the flooring replacement project.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple dented cans within the dry storage area. Discussed with PIC. This was noted during the last routine inspection on 1/19/22. Ensure staff is aware to check cans before putting on shelving units. Repeat violation.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

Observed multiple dented cans within the dry storage area. Discussed with PIC. This was noted during the last routine inspection in the General Comments as an issue. Ensure staff is aware to check cans for dents when food inventory has arrived.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the spray nozzle near the dish machine to have a build-up on grime and food debris on top of and on the squeezer of the nozzle. Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces. This was noted in the General Comments of the last routine inspection. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

(REPEAT) Observed no heat test strips and/or maximum registering thermometer for the heated dish machine. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/31/20. Inspector will follow-up on 6/18/21.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed facility lack an ability to test the heat dish machine. Facility must have heat test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer available. Discussed purchasing such items with PIC. PIC will order and contact inspector. Inspector will follow-up on 2/10/20.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11  (P) Cleaner spray bottles are stored next to back up sugar shaker and creamer bottle. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11. Foods were moved to proper storage location.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Sanitizer was remade to have 200ppm of Quat. Take care not to cross wiping cloths at area with soap and sanitizer buckets.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination at bottom cabinets in the drink area. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11. Cups observed to be out of sleeves. Keep sincle use items protected at all times. Cups were discarded.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling watermelon is inadequate. Observed containers of cut melon to be stacked 3 tall so that it is 6 inches deep. The melon containers were moved to two tall for 4 inches. The melon was also moved to the walk in cooler. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) Observed wet wiping cloths to be held on the counter top between uses. Wet wiping cloth bucket will be provided at prep line.  In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution between uses. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text: 3-302.15  (Pf )Observed soil on watermelon that is in the process of being cut. Thouroughly clean all melon (along with other fruits and vegetables) before cutting or serving. Next melons were more carefully washed. Produce is not properly washed before use. Raw fruits and vegetables shall be thoroughly washed to remove contaminants before use. Reference 3-302.15.
